preview.note: Port 5173 was occupied. A clean Vite server on port 5187 served the Supabase-free preview.

environment.browser: Headless Chrome on Windows, ANGLE D3D11 on Intel Arc 140V
environment.measurement: Three.js renderer counters for one complete garden frame, including shadow and post-processing passes. The detail view was closed. Frame intervals are requestAnimationFrame samples, not GPU timings.

checks.placement: All fixture positions matched between modes. Two cozy plants used the Blender asset and the matched cozy control stayed procedural. Other plants kept their triangle counts.
checks.selection: Canvas pointer events opened the correct Blender peony, procedural peony, pair and tree detail previews.
checks.growth: A planted peony's outer ring expanded from 0.34 to 1.0 at its exported pivot. Existing plants kept their transforms when the new plant was added and removed.
checks.lod: Mouse-wheel zoom switched between 1,796 and 566 triangles. Both levels retained the same tint material and final pose. Only one five-mesh hierarchy was attached per plant. With projected widths 60, 41, 33, 41 and 50 CSS pixels, the sequence was near, near, far, far, near.
checks.color: Pink and jade fixture peonies produced distinct opal tints while keeping the GLB materials' clearcoat, iridescence and vertex colors.
checks.navigation: Pointer dragging orbited the garden without selecting a plant. The island fit the 390 by 844 portrait viewport.
checks.resources: Chrome requested each GLB once through mode switches, selection and density changes. A new same-color plant shared the geometry and tint material. Removing it preserved both resources for the surviving plant. The tint material disposed after its last user left.
checks.failures: Blocking the hero GLB restored procedural garden and detail models. Blocking the distant GLB kept the hero available at all distances.
checks.runtime: Zero uncaught browser exceptions. The existing Three.js Clock deprecation and Vite bundle-size warning remain. Mobile framing was emulated on desktop hardware.
